masseng_boundary.used: standalone synthetic demonstration (NOT MASSENG v5 output)
masseng_boundary.note: affordability/progression are inside MASSENG v5; these numbers are an equation demonstration, not a MASSENG run. Borrowing is NOT implemented in MASSENG v5; the credit-constrained spec is synthetic only.

label: SIMULATION - stipulated household demand DGP; no causal claim
plain_result: Family income raises schooling demand in every budget specification (income elasticity range 0.16-1.51), forgone earnings reduce it, and at zero schooling effect on births the raw schooling-births association is absorbed once income is controlled. This is a demonstration of budget arithmetic, not an estimate of any country's demand.

data_map.observed: no usable public household demand micro panel (DHS IR gated; no fees/forgone panel)

statistical_frame.estimand: income elasticity of schooling demand by level; schooling-births association
statistical_frame.identification: none (simulation); zero-signal control separates strength from income
statistical_frame.testable_restrictions: budget adds up; credit binds only in that spec
statistical_frame.benchmark_split: Monte Carlo reps; no observed split
statistical_frame.pass_fail: PASS if income elasticity positive across specs and zero-signal absorbed by income control
